correctness.rationale: The Fryš--Kotrbatý simplex formula is exactly the stated degree-\(np\) Bernstein polynomial after absorbing the common \((1-t)^{n(p-1)}\) factor. Its Bernstein coefficients are \(a_j=\binom nj\) through \(j=n\) and zero afterwards. Differentiation gives coefficient differences \(a_{j+1}-a_j\), whose nonzero signs change exactly once. After \(x=t/(1-t)\), positive binomial multipliers preserve that single sign change, so Descartes gives at most one positive derivative zero. The constant coefficient is \(n-1>0\) and the last nonzero coefficient is negative, forcing one zero and a positive-to-negative derivative transition. The planar quadratic, critical point, maximum simplification and limits follow by direct algebra. The source's proved low-dimensional coefficientwise higher-order Godbersen inequality then gives the uniform-in-parameter convex-body bound for \(n\le3\). I independently checked the sign-change property for \(2\le n\le20\) and representative orders, while the inspected verifier checks the same identities on a broader finite grid; the all-parameter theorem rests on the symbolic sign argument.
